meta.purpose: THE PREPARATION STAGE. Process raw into the substrate the lexical read needs — the span master, the stem master, the char seed, and passages — and hand it over under signoff. Everything here is mechanical: derivation, never judgement.

the_researcher_model.quote: researcher 2026-07-15: 'the registry create the starting point... raw pulls STEP and create the tables with the STEP data. No data conversion. Base then processes the data and prepare it for the lexical analysis. This requires master, char seed, and passages to be in place. With signoff of the base, the lexical analysis can start.'
the_researcher_model.the_stage_chain: REGISTRY (the starting point) -> RAW (STEP data, no conversion) -> BASE (process it into what lexical needs) -> [SIGNOFF] -> LEXICAL -> CHARACTERISTICS -> FINDINGS
the_researcher_model.what_this_settled: open.pipeline.base-layer-carve. Base is ONE process, not three. I had recommended three (spans / stems / passages) on the grounds that they are unrelated derivations. That was wrong, and the reason is instructive: I carved by WHAT IS PRODUCED; the researcher carves by WHEN IT IS DONE. A stage is a unit of completion — these four artefacts always run together, always for the same scope, and are only ever FINISHED together, because they finish at one signoff. That is what makes them one process.
the_researcher_model.the_signoff_is_the_boundary: 'With signoff of the base, the lexical analysis can start' is not a nicety — it is what makes base a stage rather than a bag of derivations. A stage has an end. This one's end is a human decision.

meta.envelope: Every item carries the common rule envelope — see ../_manifest.json meta.envelope.
meta.supersedes: `verses-passages` — retired 2026-07-15. Passages are a base OUTPUT, not a process of their own; treating one artefact of this stage as a peer of the stage was the carve error.
meta.the_layer_rule: Base is DERIVATION. Raw is what STEP said (no conversion); base is what we computed from it; interpretation is what we judged. Nothing in this file may contain a judgement — if a rule here needs to decide what something MEANS, it is in the wrong layer.

nodes.process: The stage's rules — what it derives, in what order, and the signoff that ends it.
nodes.entities: What it owns: the span master, the stem master, the candidate seed, passages.
nodes.output: The base review pack — what the researcher signs off.
nodes.validation: The gates, including the signoff gate that releases lexical.

open.issue: The signoff is a HUMAN gate — the only one in the pipeline so far. How is it recorded, what is its scope, and what invalidates it?
open.why_it_matters: A signoff nobody can point at is not a control. And a signoff that survives its evidence changing is worse than none: it launders a stale approval into apparent authority.
questions: SCOPE — per book? per scope-of-run? A book-level signoff is the natural unit (base runs per book), but a partial re-run then leaves the signoff covering data it never saw.
INVALIDATION — a re-pull can correct raw (raw.step-precedence). Does that void the base signoff for that scope? It must, or the signoff attests to evidence that no longer exists.
RECORD — who, when, on what evidence, at which cfg_version. Same requirement as any ruling (meta.open.decision-provenance).
open.recommendation: Per book; recorded with who/when/cfg_version + a hash of the base outputs it covers; AUTO-VOIDED when any input beneath it changes. The hash is what makes invalidation mechanical rather than remembered — the researcher signs off on a specific state, and if the state moves, the signature no longer matches it. That is the difference between a control and a habit.
open.resolve_by: researcher decision — needed before base can actually gate lexical

open.issue: The seed is deliberately over-inclusive and non-exhaustive — Screen 0 then rejects. But there is no rule for what over-inclusive MEANS, so the seed's breadth is a judgement made per run. (Carried from characteristics.json; the seed lives here now.)
open.consequence: Seed breadth silently sets the study's coverage. Too narrow and the inner being is understated — precisely what the two prior ~100-page studies did, and the quality bar this programme measures itself against.
open.recommendation: Bias to over-inclusion and let Screen 0 carry the cost: a false positive is caught by a gate; a false negative is invisible forever. State it as a rule with a measurable seed-recall check (gate.char.seed-recall).

open.issue: No stem-master table exists in the live DB (plan §4: 'No dedicated stem-master table exists — derive from verse_morphology'). This is a new build, and it is unclear whether the master is a persisted table or a derived view.
open.recommendation: PERSISTED. A derive-on-demand view cannot be signed off, cannot be gated, and cannot carry provenance — and base's whole shape is 'produce it, prove it, sign it off'. Also carried in the plan's parking lot ('Stem-master: first-class persisted table vs derive-on-demand').

open.issue: base.cluster-assignment is declared not-re-run, but gate.base.regenerable requires base to reproduce exactly when regenerated. A never-re-run assignment cannot be proved that way — and if it were re-run against a changed cluster population it might not reproduce.
open.recommendation: Treat the ASSIGNMENT as regenerable (the rule is stated, so it can be re-derived and compared) but never automatically OVERWRITE an existing one — re-derivation reports a divergence for the researcher rather than silently reassigning. That keeps the gate honest without re-litigating settled membership.

process.subject: base-definition
process.authority: researcher ruling 2026-07-16 — 'base has several interpretive operations: seeding characteristics in master, cluster assignment, passage inclusion etc. regeneration of base should be possible if the config rules in base is followed. base feed off the raw STEP data, but is certainly not purely mechanical without judgements.'
process.intent: Define base as the RULE-GOVERNED derivation stage between raw and interpretation. Base judges — which spans to look at, where a passage breaks, which cluster a term joins — but every judgement follows a rule stated in this config, which is what makes base regenerable.
process.satisfaction: Every base row is reproducible by following a rule stated in this component, without reading what the text means.

spec.statement: Base = what we DERIVED from raw by a stated rule. Raw = what STEP SAID (no conversion). Interpretation = what we JUDGED by reading meaning. Base judges, but only where a rule governs the judgement.
spec.the_test: Can this row be reproduced by following a rule stated in this config, without reading what the text MEANS? Yes -> base. Needs the source -> raw. Needs a reading of meaning -> interpretation.
spec.regenerable_not_migrated: Base is REGENERATED, never migrated (plan §3.4.1: 'Base — derived: passages, stems, seed/candidate stamping | Regenerate | deterministic; rebuilt by the modules, never migrated'). A base layer that had to be migrated would be admitting it is not derivable — and then it is not base.

★ the_correction_20260716.what_v1_said: 'everything the lexical read needs, computed from raw, with NO JUDGEMENT anywhere in it'.
★ the_correction_20260716.why_it_was_wrong: Base already housed three judgements when that was written: base.char-seed (which spans are worth reading), base.passages (where the reading unit breaks) and now base.cluster-assignment. Both existing ones already declared axis C -- they were being treated as rule-governed judgements while the definition denied judgement existed.
★ the_correction_20260716.the_tell: base.char-seed carried a spec key named `the_judgement_layer_in_the_name`, arguing that a seed layer literally called 'judgement' was 'a judgement about WHAT TO LOOK AT, not about what anything MEANS'. That is a rule defended by exception. The exception is now the rule: base judges, under a stated rule.
★ the_correction_20260716.what_regenerable_now_means: STRONGER, not weaker. Regeneration is the test that the rule was really written down: if base cannot be reproduced by following this config, the rule is missing or underspecified. gate.base.regenerable is unchanged and now has teeth.
★ the_correction_20260716.what_the_signoff_attests: not 'this was mechanical' but 'these rules were followed'.
★ the_correction_20260716.no_api: A base judgement must not require the model (researcher 2026-07-16: 'the judgements should not require any Claude API, but it is not impossible - although I would be surprised'). Base judgements are axis C: a stated rule, executed in code, escalating to the RESEARCHER -- never to the model -- when the rule cannot decide.

process.subject: span-master
process.authority: researcher 2026-07-15 (base 'requires master... to be in place'); plan §3.4.2 ('the span-id is the join key')
process.intent: ★ Mint the currency everything above is addressed in. Derive, from raw morphology, one addressable span per term-in-verse — the join key for every lexical read, every candidate, and every pair endpoint.
process.satisfaction: Every term-in-verse in scope has exactly one span, carrying a resolved span_strong_match, resolving to a real verse and a real term.

spec.statement: The span master is derived from raw morphology: one addressable row per term-in-verse. It is THE join key — never Strong's-encoded endpoints (plan §3.4.2).
what_depends_on_it: the candidate seed — a candidate IS a span
span_strong_match — the field that proves a term is actually AT a verse: the difference between evidence and a reference
spec.⚠ today_it_is_a_side_effect: audit_word 'inserts + span-links terms and verses in one pass', reachable via `--skip-span-backpop`. A step everything joins on is currently SKIPPABLE, ungated, and has no process. That is the pre-processing the researcher identified as missing.
spec.the_layer_correction: Span-linking sits inside the ingest module today, which puts a DERIVED artefact inside a raw process. Spans are computed, therefore base. Moving them here is not tidying — it is what lets them be gated and signed off.

process.subject: stem-master
process.authority: researcher 2026-07-15 (base 'requires master... to be in place'); plan §3.3.4 (module 4)
process.intent: Build the stem master from morphology, so the lexical read's morphological dimensions have a canonical derivation to rely on rather than re-deriving per read.
process.satisfaction: Every attested stem is in the master, derived from morph_code, with no stem invented and none missing.

spec.statement: The stem master is derived from morph_code. Morphology is the source of truth; the stem is its derivation, never the reverse.
spec.the_authority_direction: morph_code -> stem. Anything contradicting morph_code is wrong, including the registry (memory project_morph_is_source_of_truth: language was buggily derived from the Strong's PREFIX, which is blind to Aramaic — 121 terms were relabelled Hebrew->Aramaic once morph became authoritative).
spec.new_build: No stem-master table exists in the live DB (plan §4). This is not a rewrite of an existing script — see open.base.stem-master-shape.

process.subject: candidate-seed
process.authority: researcher 2026-07-15 (base 'requires... char seed... to be in place'); cycle authoritative v1 §4A; plan §3.4.1 (seed = base)
process.intent: Nominate the spans worth reading, through widening layers, biased to over-inclusion — because Screen 0 can reject a false positive but nothing can recover a span never seeded.
process.satisfaction: The seed is built through all layers, is over-inclusive and explicitly non-exhaustive, and every candidate resolves to a verse-record.

spec.stance: OVER-INCLUSIVE and NON-EXHAUSTIVE. The seed nominates; it does not pre-judge.
spec.rationale: A false positive costs one gate call. A false negative is invisible forever — and understating the inner being is the exact failure of the two prior studies this programme measures itself against.
spec.moved_from: process/characteristics.json (2026-07-15) — the seed is BASE (plan §3.4.1); an interpretation process was holding a base artefact.
spec.⚠ the_layer_split_this_forces: WHICH spans are candidates = mechanical, base, here. WHAT a candidate IS (Screen 0, role) = judgement, interpretation, characteristics. They were two facts on one row — and that co-location is exactly what the migration strips (the live DB stamps role/char_candidate onto verse_span_index).
spec.⚠ the_judgement_layer_in_the_name: Seed layer 3 is literally called 'judgement', which sits oddly in a no-judgement stage. It is a judgement about WHAT TO LOOK AT, not about what anything MEANS — a scope decision, not a reading. Base may decide where to point; it may never decide what it sees.

process.subject: passage-construction
process.authority: researcher 2026-07-15 (base 'requires... passages to be in place'); passage rule v2 (candidate-driven)
process.intent: Build the reading unit: a passage is a maximal run of consecutive candidate-bearing verses, anchored at its first verse.
process.satisfaction: Every candidate-bearing verse belongs to exactly one passage; coverage arithmetic reconciles; no passage is a whole long chapter.

spec.rule: v2, candidate-driven: a maximal run of CONSECUTIVE candidate-bearing verses. Anchor = the first verse. Single-verse passages are allowed. No whole-chapter passages.
spec.depends_on: base.char-seed — a passage is defined BY candidates, so the seed must exist first
spec.genre_routing: Treatment varies by genre (poetic two-phase vs narrative cross-verse vs discourse segmentation) — the routing rule is lexical.genre-routing; this rule builds the passages, it does not decide how they are read.
spec.why_never_a_whole_chapter: The reading unit is the passage precisely so that the read stays bounded and grounded. A whole-chapter 'passage' is how depth drifts into skim (memory feedback_read_by_passage_not_whole_chapter).
spec.was: the `verses-passages` process — retired 2026-07-15; passages are a base OUTPUT, not a process.

process.subject: base-signoff
process.authority: researcher ruling 2026-07-15: 'With signoff of the base, the lexical analysis can start.'
process.intent: ★ The stage boundary. Base is not done when its modules finish — it is done when the researcher signs it off. Lexical does not start before that.
process.satisfaction: A signed-off base for the scope, covering the state that actually exists.

spec.statement: The lexical analysis MAY NOT START until base is signed off for its scope. Signoff is a researcher act, not a module outcome.
what_is_signed_off: and the gates over all four
spec.why_a_human_gate_here_and_nowhere_else: Base is the last point where a defect is CHEAP. Everything after it is interpretation: an error in the span master or the seed does not surface as a bad span — it surfaces as a wrong reading, months later, indistinguishable from a bad read. The 2026-07-14 audit could not tell those apart, which is exactly why it took an acceptance sample to find anything.
spec.it_is_also_the_scope_decision: Signoff is where the researcher accepts the seed's breadth — and seed breadth silently sets what the study can ever find (open.base.seed-over-inclusive). Signing off base IS accepting the coverage. That should be visible at the moment of signing, not discovered later.
spec.⚠ note: RECONCILE — the MECHANISM is undecided (scope, record, invalidation). The RULE is not in question: the researcher ruled it. What is open is how a signoff is recorded and what voids it.
spec.the_invalidation_problem: raw.step-precedence means raw CAN change under a signed-off base. A signoff that survives its evidence changing is worse than no signoff — it launders a stale approval into apparent authority. See open.base.signoff-mechanism.

process.subject: term-cluster-membership
process.authority: researcher 2026-07-16 — 'check if the term has a cluster, if not, check if the term naturally belong in a cluster by comparing the terms in clusters — this assignment is done on the basis of a loose relationship and it is a judgement call. In the unlikely event that no cluster can be found, then it is flushed back to researcher for a decision.'
process.intent: Put every term in an analysis group. A cluster is defined by the terms already in it, so membership is decided by comparing the candidate term against those members — a loose relationship, judged under this rule, never a reading of the term's meaning.
process.satisfaction: Every term either carries a cluster, or carries a recorded escalation to the researcher. Nothing is left silently unassigned.

spec.trigger: a new term is added. Not run otherwise.
procedure: 1. [C] Does the term already carry a cluster? -> done. Membership is not re-decided.
2. [C] Compare the term against THE TERMS IN EACH CLUSTER. Where it relates loosely to a cluster's members, it joins that cluster.
3. [C] No cluster found -> ESCALATE TO THE RESEARCHER. Do not guess, do not create a cluster, do not leave it null and silent.
spec.★ what_loose_relationship_means: The comparison is TERM-TO-TERM against a cluster's existing members — a cluster has no definition apart from the terms in it. The relatedness is already in hand: STEP returns relatedNos, rawRelatedNumbers and definitions[] on the pull the term arrived through, and the root family derives from them. So 'does this term relate to that cluster's terms' is set overlap over data the study already holds — which is why this needs no model.
spec.axis_note: C. The judgement is real but it is RULED, and the escalation path goes to the RESEARCHER, never to the model (researcher 2026-07-16: 'the judgements should not require any Claude API').
spec.is_not_re_run: Researcher 2026-07-16: 'It is highly unlikely that the term-cluster membership will ever be re-run.' An isolated process, called on the trigger. This is the one base artefact that is not rebuilt wholesale — see open.base.cluster-regenerability.
spec.why_base_and_not_raw: It is not a raw-data determination (researcher 2026-07-16). Raw is what STEP said; which analysis group a term joins is derived. It is not interpretation either: it reads no meaning, it compares terms.
spec.the_live_model: mti_terms.cluster_code (49 clusters, M01..M47 + FLAG + T2) is the term->cluster edge; cluster_subgroup / mti_term_subgroup carry the sub-group placement. The model exists; the method did not.
spec.history: Researcher 2026-07-16: 'I guess you handled it by hook or by crook in the past by simply chatting and then updating, some of it I channeled through AI chat.' This entry is the method it never had.

entities.subject: span
entities.intent: The addressable term-in-verse — the join key for the entire interpretation layer.
entities.satisfaction: One row per term-in-verse; resolves to a verse and a term; carries span_strong_match.

does_not_hold: role · char_candidate · characteristic · ib_char_id — INTERPRETATION. The live DB stamps these onto verse_span_index; the migration strips them (plan 3.4.1).
spec.note: The one entity every other layer's identity is built from.

entities.subject: stem-master
entities.intent: The canonical stem inventory, derived from morphology.
entities.satisfaction: One row per attested stem, derived from morph_code.

spec.note: ⚠ Does not exist in the live DB (plan §4). New build; persisted-vs-derived undecided.

entities.subject: candidate
entities.intent: A span nominated for reading — a question, not an assertion. Seeded over-inclusively; Screen 0 decides whether it survives.
entities.satisfaction: One row per nominated span, each resolving to a verse-record.

does_not_hold: the Screen-0 verdict · role — INTERPRETATION, and they live in process/characteristics.json. This is the layer split base.char-seed forces.

entities.subject: passage
entities.intent: The reading unit — a maximal run of consecutive candidate-bearing verses.
entities.satisfaction: One row per passage; anchored at its first verse; every candidate-bearing verse belongs to exactly one.

spec.grain: one row per maximal candidate-bearing run
spec.note: verse.passage_id / is_passage_anchor / genre sit ON the verse row in the live DB — which mixes raw and base on one row (flagged in ent.raw.verse). The new schema separates them, or raw's immutability cannot hold.

entities.subject: cluster
entities.authority: researcher 2026-07-16 — 'check if the term has a cluster, if not, check if the term naturally belong in a cluster by comparing the terms in clusters — this assignment is done on the basis of a loose relationship and it is a judgement call. In the unlikely event that no cluster can be found, then it is flushed back to researcher for a decision.'
entities.intent: The analysis group — a collection of terms studied together. It has no definition apart from its members, which is why membership is decided against them.
entities.satisfaction: Every cluster resolves to at least one term; every term resolves to at most one cluster.

spec.the_edge: term -> cluster is one edge (mti_terms.cluster_code). A term has at most one cluster.
spec.sub_groups: cluster_subgroup / mti_term_subgroup carry placement WITHIN a cluster — a separate, finer question this rule does not decide.
spec.layer: base — the membership is derived; the cluster list itself is researcher-owned

output.subject: base-review-pack
output.authority: base.signoff; plan §3.6 ('Reviews — for the researcher to sign off')
output.intent: The artefact the researcher signs off — what base built, what it covers, and what it chose not to.
output.satisfaction: Every base run for a scope produces a review pack sufficient to sign off or reject on.

must_include: span master — count, span_strong_match distribution, unresolved spans
stem master — stems derived, any morph_code that produced none
char seed — candidates by seed layer, and THE BREADTH (signing off base is accepting the coverage)
passages — count, verse coverage arithmetic, any whole-chapter or orphan verse
what was NOT covered — and why
spec.why_red: There is no signoff without something to sign off ON. A verbal 'base looks fine' is the habit this gate replaces.

validation.subject: base-signoff
validation.intent: ★ Hold lexical until base is signed off for its scope. The pipeline's only human gate.
validation.satisfaction: A valid, current signoff exists for the scope lexical is about to read.

spec.on_fail: HALT. Lexical does not start. Not a warning, not a prompt — the stage boundary is the control.
spec.note: The RULE is ruled; the MECHANISM (scope, record, what voids it) is open. A signoff that cannot be invalidated when its evidence changes is not a control.

validation.subject: span-master
validation.intent: Refuse a span master with holes — because a missing span is not a missing row, it is a verse the study can never read.
validation.satisfaction: Every term-in-verse in scope has a span; every span carries span_strong_match; no orphans.

checks: every term-in-verse has exactly one span
no span orphaned from its verse or term
spec.why_it_matters_most: This gate is the reason spans became a process. Bundled inside audit_word behind --skip-span-backpop, span completeness had no gate at all — and everything above it joins on its output.

validation.subject: base-definition
validation.authority: base.definition; plan §3.4.1 ('deterministic; rebuilt by the modules, never migrated')
validation.intent: Prove base is genuinely derived — regenerating it from raw must reproduce it exactly.
validation.satisfaction: A regeneration from raw reproduces the base layer identically.

spec.why: If base cannot be regenerated from raw, something in it was not derived — it was entered, judged, or inherited. This gate is what keeps the layer honest, and it is the same test the plan applies to the migration ('regenerate everything deterministic').
spec.note: Also the cheapest possible check on the correction-cascade (open.raw.correction-cascade): if raw changed, regeneration DIVERGES, and the divergence is exactly the set of base rows a raw correction invalidated.

validation.subject: base-judgement-is-ruled
validation.intent: Require every judgement in base to name the config rule that governs it — so base stays regenerable and the signoff attests to rules followed, not to a mechanical warrant it never had.
validation.satisfaction: Every base row produced by a judgement names its governing rule id; no base row carries a reading of meaning.

spec.the_known_violation: The live DB stamps role / char_candidate / characteristic / ib_char_id onto verse_span_index. Those name no rule AND are readings of meaning — this gate still catches them, on both counts.
spec.why_it_matters_here_specifically: Base is signed off AS MECHANICAL. A judgement smuggled into base is a judgement that gets a researcher's signature without ever being screened.
spec.★ recast_20260716: WAS 'no-interpretive-fields' — keep interpretation out of base. That was wrong: base legitimately judges (char-seed, passages, cluster-assignment). Banning judgement would have required parking three of base's own LIVE rules. The gate now bans UNRULED judgement, which is the thing that was actually dangerous.
spec.what_it_no_longer_catches: A rule-governed base judgement. That is correct: it is what base is for.

validation.subject: term-cluster-membership
validation.authority: researcher 2026-07-16 — 'check if the term has a cluster, if not, check if the term naturally belong in a cluster by comparing the terms in clusters — this assignment is done on the basis of a loose relationship and it is a judgement call. In the unlikely event that no cluster can be found, then it is flushed back to researcher for a decision.'
validation.intent: Catch a term with no cluster and no escalation — a term the study holds but no analysis group owns, which is how a term goes silently unstudied.
validation.satisfaction: For every term: cluster_code is set, OR an escalation to the researcher is recorded.

spec.on_fail: halt — an unassigned, unescalated term is invisible to the analysis
spec.note: This is the check a per-word registry signoff would read: a word is not signed off until every one of its terms passes this gate. The registry signoff itself is the researcher's to define (2026-07-16: 'I will separately deal with registry').

naming.subject: base-ids
naming.satisfaction: Base rule ids use the declared prefixes.

filing.subject: base-filing
filing.intent: Where this process's artefacts are filed.
filing.satisfaction: Base outputs land in the declared tree; superseded versions archived.

implemented_by.note: The PIPELINE says WHEN this process runs and in what units; THIS FILE says what its rules are. Two axes over one thing (plan §A.11): a module loads its governing rule-set before it runs, and this is that rule-set. Added 2026-07-15 so the two are navigable in both directions.
implemented_by.authority: researcher ruling 2026-07-15 — align the process files with the pipeline's terminology; the terminology belongs in the enums (ruling a)
